description: Adversaries may attempt to exploit a software vulnerability (such as buffer overflows, path traversal, or Remote Code Execution) in an internet-facing service to gain an initial foothold. This profile captures the network signature of the exploit delivery phase, often followed immediately by the establishment of a persistent, interactive reverse-shell or secondary payload download.

patterns.description: Anomalies related to the physical size of the packets used to deliver the exploit code.

features.name: Anomalous Maximum Packet Length
features.description: The attack often involves sending a highly specialized, oversized packet (High Max Packet Length) to trigger a buffer overflow or deliver a compiled exploit payload in a single, massive request.

features.name: Low Forward Packet Volume
features.description: Unlike volumetric attacks, successful infiltration often requires very few packets. A precise exploit may only need a handful of forward packets (Low Total Fwd Pkts) to compromise the target.

patterns.description: Metrics highlighting how the connection is maintained after the initial exploit succeeds.

features.name: Extended Flow Longevity
features.description: Once the exploit succeeds, the connection often transitions into an interactive reverse-shell or command session, keeping the network flow open indefinitely (High Flow Duration).

features.name: Erratic Inter-Arrival Times
features.description: A high variance in the time between forward packets (High Fwd IAT Std) strongly suggests an interactive session where a human attacker is typing commands, causing irregular pauses, rather than a steady automated script.

patterns.description: Characteristics of the flow rate and the targeted services.

features.name: Stealthy Packet Transmission Rate
features.description: The overall rate of packets per second (Low Flow Pkts/s) remains very low to evade rate-limiting and threshold-based IDS alerts.

features.name: Atypical Service Communication
features.description: The exploit may target any vulnerable service (represented by a randomized or unspecified typical port), or the resulting bind-shell may open on a non-standard, high-numbered ephemeral port to await the attacker's connection.

patterns.description: Indicators for distinguishing malicious infiltration from benign administrative activity.

features.name: Interactive Admin Resemblance (False Positive Filtering)
features.description: Legitimate administrative tools (like SSH, RDP, or PowerShell Remoting) naturally exhibit high flow durations, erratic typing timings, and variable packet lengths, potentially mimicking a post-infiltration reverse shell.

features.name: Software Update Signatures
features.description: Specialized software updates pulling large initial payloads over atypical ports can occasionally trigger similar maximum packet length and duration alerts.
